title: pin tumbler lock
description: A notched key lifts four spring-loaded pin stacks until every split sits on the shear line; no door, handle or lock casing shown

facts.intro: Introduce a recognizable pin tumbler lock: a red-handled key resting outside a dark lock body, with four brass and steel pins standing in a row under four springs. A bright brass line runs across the body.
facts.cutaway: A simplified cutaway lifts the cover to expose the four brass pins, the four steel pins above them, the four springs and the brass line across the body.
facts.drive: An illustrated push slides the key into the lock. Its notched top rides under each brass pin and lifts it by a different height.
facts.response: The key goes all the way in. Each pin has been lifted just enough, so the gap between each brass pin and steel pin sits exactly on the brass line.
facts.hold: No part moves for this explanation. The four brass pins have four different lengths, and the four notches in the key have four matching depths.
facts.repeat: The key is pulled part of the way out. Without it the springs push every pin back down, so no gap is left on the brass line.
facts.limit: The key slides back in. As the notches pass under each pin the springs let them rise and fall until the gaps reach the line again.
facts.payoff: The cover closes. Key, pins and springs work together: only a key with the right notches lines up every gap. No door is shown.

narration_rules.message: no door or lock picking is depicted; speak only of the key, pins and springs
